Phosphorylation of FG-nucleoporin NUP98 as an early initiator of nuclear-import failure and nuclear TDP-43 loss in TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS motor neurons

Hypothesis. In spinal motor neurons with TDP-43 proteinopathy, the pathologic pattern common in sporadic ALS, phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin NUP98 is proposed as an early, pore-intrinsic initiating event. The modification is hypothesized to slow facilitated nuclear import, lower nuclear TDP-43, and promote further cytoplasmic TDP-43 accumulation. Later structural injury of nuclear pores and sequestration of mobile transport factors are treated as downstream amplifiers. The proposal applies to this TDP-43-proteinopathy context. A shared initiating phosphorylation step for C9orf72 ALS is outside the claim.

Supported premises. Insoluble TDP-43 associates with nuclear-pore and transport components. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in cell systems, and related pore pathology occurs in ALS tissue [S1]. The chemistry and the cross-subtype sequence remain unspecified [S1]. Cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form independently of conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport-associated proteins, and accompany import failure, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death [S3]. Phosphorylated species in that study are phosphorylated TDP-43, a different substrate from a nucleoporin [S3]. Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA is linked to RanGAP mislocalization and impaired nuclear import, and changing transport or repeat-RNA mechanisms modifies model phenotypes [S2]. Cellular stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs transport, and changing stress-granule assembly modifies those phenotypes [S4]. [S3] and [S4] together supply a sequestration route and show that conventional stress granules are dispensable for some TDP-43-linked transport defects. Nucleoporin phosphorylation is not an established cause in any of these sources.

Speculative bridges. The kinase, the phosphorylated residues, and the selection of NUP98 are assumptions. Unverified prior knowledge, absent from [S1]-[S4], holds that proline-directed kinases phosphorylate FG-nucleoporins, including NUP98, during mitotic nuclear-pore remodeling, and that such phosphorylation can loosen the selectivity barrier in dividing cells. The ALS-specific bridge is that a persistent neuronal stress kinase in that class phosphorylates NUP98 molecules already assembled in post-mitotic motor-neuron pores. That change is proposed to delay import of shuttling TDP-43 while the pore scaffold remains and before karyopherins are trapped in granules or TDP-43 assemblies. The proposed order runs from neuronal stress and early cytoplasmic TDP-43 imbalance to NUP98 phosphorylation, selective import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, growth of cytoplasmic assemblies, and only later karyopherin and Ran-regulator sequestration plus structural pore disruption [S1][S3]. Phosphorylation is the candidate initiator. Assembly-driven mislocalization is the candidate downstream response.

Alternative explanations. Stress-granule capture of transport factors can impair import with NUP98 phosphorylation absent or incidental [S4]. Stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can recruit those factors and block import on their own [S3]. In C9orf72 neurons, RanGAP mislocalization can explain the transport phenotype, with NUP98 phosphorylation a later correlate [S2]. Phosphorylation could also arise only after import has failed, reporting damage rather than starting it. Widespread proteostatic stress could drive death, with transport changes as a parallel consequence.

Discriminating test. The test uses human iPSC-derived spinal motor neurons carrying a TDP-43 mutation or a controlled induction of cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies, alongside isogenic controls, sampled before cell death. A C9orf72 neuron line is included only as a boundary contrast. In the same cultures, map nuclear-envelope NUP98 phosphosites by mass spectrometry of pore-enriched fractions; quantify a nuclear-import reporter, the nuclear-to-cytoplasmic TDP-43 ratio, G3BP1 stress granules, one karyopherin, and RanGAP. Three perturbations at near-endogenous expression then separate mechanisms. Phospho-null NUP98 at the mapped sites should preserve import and nuclear TDP-43 during a stress that still forms stress granules. Phosphomimetic NUP98 in healthy neurons should slow import and reduce nuclear TDP-43 when stress-granule assembly is blocked. Forced cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies should be induced on the phospho-null background. Recovery of import while assemblies or granules remain would favor a pore-intrinsic requirement. Recovery only after granules disperse, with phosphorylation still present, would favor sequestration [S4].

Falsifying observation. The hypothesis is falsified in this cellular context if NUP98 phosphorylation fails to precede import slowing and nuclear TDP-43 loss, if phosphomimetic NUP98 leaves both import and nuclear TDP-43 unchanged when stress granules are absent, or if phospho-null NUP98 leaves import impaired whenever cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies or stress granules are present. Phosphorylation that appears only after karyopherin sequestration, and phosphosite alleles that do not move the transport phenotypes, would reclassify the modification as a downstream correlate.

Limitations. Kinase identity, residue positions, and the focus on NUP98 remain assumptions until mapping is done; a different FG-nucleoporin may be the relevant substrate. Phosphomimetic substitutions approximate charge and can miss kinase-dependent binding partners. iPSC motor neurons omit long aging, glia, and neuromuscular circuitry. A positive result would remain specific to TDP-43 proteinopathy and would leave the C9orf72 route unresolved [S2]. The design tests a hypothesis rather than a treatment.

Hypothesis title: Early Nup62 phosphorylation initiates nuclear-import failure in TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS, upstream of transport-factor sequestration.

Hypothesis and context. In TDP-43 proteinopathy, the pathology typical of most sporadic ALS, phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup62 is an initiating, pore-intrinsic cause of selective nuclear-import failure. Import failure then depletes nuclear TDP-43, favors persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies, and only later recruits transport-factor sequestration as an amplifier. The same sequence is not proposed as the initiating route in C9orf72 repeat-expansion ALS.

Supported premises. Insoluble TDP-43 aggregates associate with nuclear-pore and transport components; disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cells, and related pore pathology is present in ALS tissue [S1]. These observations support a TDP-43–pore connection. They leave the initiating biochemical event unidentified. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form independently of conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport-associated proteins, and accompany impaired import, loss of nuclear TDP-43, and cell death; phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulates in those assemblies [S3]. That phosphorylation is of TDP-43, which is separate from nucleoporin phosphorylation. Cellular stress also recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs nucleocytoplasmic transport, and altering stress-granule assembly modifies those defects [S4]. Together, [S3] and [S4] establish two sequestration routes, so conventional stress granules are not required for every TDP-43-linked transport defect. Expanded C9orf72 RNA is linked to RanGAP mislocalization and impaired import in models and patient neurons, a genetic-context-specific route [S2].

Initiating mechanism versus downstream response. The proposed first event is phosphorylation of Nup62. Nup62 is treated here as a central-channel FG-nucleoporin (identity and channel role: unverified prior knowledge; the packet does not name the nucleoporin). The modification is hypothesized to weaken FG-repeat cohesion enough to slow nuclear import of TDP-43 and other cargoes. Cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies [S3] and stress-granule capture of transport factors [S4] are placed downstream, as responses that can sustain import failure after the pore modification has begun. This ordering separates an intrinsic pore alteration from sequestration and from collapse that is only secondary to broad cellular stress.

Speculative bridges. No supplied source names a kinase, a residue, or a direct Nup62 interaction. The following are assumptions. A stress-responsive proline-directed kinase, with ERK1/2 as a candidate (unverified prior knowledge that ERK can phosphorylate nucleoporins), modifies an FG-domain site on Nup62 before import failure is measurable. Phospho-Nup62 is sufficient to impair import while stress-granule dynamics remain intact. The same site is occupied in spinal motor neurons from TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS. These assumptions define a test; they do not establish a mechanism or a treatment.

Alternative explanations. Transport failure may be caused by sequestration of importins, exportins, or Ran regulators into stress granules [S4] or into stress-granule-independent TDP-43 assemblies [S3], with Nup62 phosphorylation appearing only afterward. In C9orf72 disease, repeat RNA may drive RanGAP mislocalization and import failure [S2] with little contribution from Nup62 phosphorylation. Nucleoporin mislocalization [S1] may be a consequence of aggregate binding or late cellular disassembly, so the phosphate mark would report damage rather than cause it. Broad proteostatic stress may also push pore phosphorylation and transport failure in parallel.

Discriminating preclinical test. In human iPSC-derived motor neurons, compare an inducible cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing paradigm aligned with the stress-granule-independent regime [S3] and an acute stress paradigm that assembles canonical stress granules [S4]. Edit endogenous NUP62 to a phospho-null allele and to a phosphomimetic allele at the pre-specified candidate site. Add a kinase-inhibitor arm only as a less selective corroboration. Across a dense time course, quantify Nup62 phospho-occupancy by targeted mass spectrometry, nucleoporin localization, a nuclear-import reporter, nuclear versus cytoplasmic TDP-43, stress-granule markers, and cell death. Cross the alleles with experimental block or preservation of stress-granule assembly so sequestration state is separable from the phospho-genotype. The initiating-pore model predicts three results: phospho-occupancy rises before the import reporter fails; phospho-null Nup62 preserves import and nuclear TDP-43 while cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies or stress granules are still present; and phosphomimetic Nup62 impairs import before those assemblies peak. The sequestration alternatives predict that import still fails in phospho-null cells whenever transport factors enter granules or TDP-43 assemblies, and that phosphomimetic Nup62 leaves import intact when those structures are prevented.

Falsifying observation. Import failure and nuclear TDP-43 loss follow the same kinetics and magnitude in phospho-null and wild-type neurons under both paradigms, or Nup62 phospho-occupancy rises only after the import reporter has already failed and the phosphomimetic leaves import intact in otherwise unstressed neurons. Either outcome reclassifies Nup62 phosphorylation as a downstream correlate.

Limitations. The nucleoporin, residue, and kinase are assumptions. Redundant phosphorylation of other FG-nucleoporins could bypass a single edit. iPSC motor neurons omit aging, glia, and circuit context. A result in TDP-43 proteinopathy would leave the C9orf72 route [S2] and other sporadic trajectories [S1] unresolved. Phosphomimetic substitutions approximate charge. The experiment tests causality and does not validate a biomarker or a therapy.

author: grok
critique: The mitotic FG-nucleoporin precedent is mismatched to the claimed mechanism: mitotic NUP98 phosphorylation is tied to pore disassembly, while the hypothesis needs a scaffold-intact import delay that S1 already borders as structural injury. Pre-register a multi-point time series with a rule that phosphosite occupancy rises first, and require phosphomimetic NUP98 to slow import in cells that still lack stress granules and karyopherin sequestration.

The same bins score the nuclear-to-cytoplasmic TDP-43 ratio, TNPO1, RanGAP, and envelope localization of NUP107 and NUP133, which must remain envelope-localized when import first slows. Phospho-null edits should preserve both reporters, the passive probe, and nuclear TDP-43 while assemblies persist. Phosphomimetic edits at the same sites, in uninduced G3BP1/2-disrupted cells, should slow both reporters, raise the passive probe, and lower nuclear TDP-43 without granules or TNPO1 or RanGAP sequestration. Matched NUP62, NUP153, and NUP214 alleles are selectivity controls. Preserved import during persistent assemblies on phospho-null NUP98 favors a pore-intrinsic step; rescue only after granules disperse would favor sequestration [S4].

Falsifying observation. Falsification is occupancy that fails to lead import slowing, passive leak, and nuclear TDP-43 loss; a flat passive probe in that same reporter bin; envelope exit of NUP107 or NUP133; matching precedence on another panel member; unchanged reporters, probe, and nuclear TDP-43 after phosphomimetic NUP98 without TNPO1 or RanGAP sequestration; impaired import on phospho-null NUP98 with assemblies still present; or occupancy only after arsenite, only in TARDBP M337V, or only after TNPO1 sequestration.

Limitations. CDK5 and the FG SP/TP list remain assumptions, and another FG-nucleoporin may be the substrate. Phosphomimetics approximate charge and can miss kinase-dependent partners. iPSC motor neurons omit long aging, glia, and neuromuscular circuitry. A positive result would remain model-specific and would leave the C9orf72 route unresolved [S2].

ranking.item: Phosphorylation of FG-nucleoporin NUP98 as an early initiator of nuclear-import failure and nuclear TDP-43 loss in TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS motor neurons

answer.answer:
Phosphorylation of an FG-repeat cluster on assembled NUP98 initiates selective nuclear-import failure before nuclear TDP-43 loss in experimental TDP-43 proteinopathy

The hypothesis is restricted to post-mitotic human neurons expressing TDP-43 M337V: phosphorylation of a mass-spectrometry-locked FG-repeat serine/threonine cluster on pore-assembled NUP98 initiates selective karyopherin-mediated import failure. C9orf72-linked disease and sporadic ALS are comparison boundaries. The claimed sequence applies to experimental TDP-43 proteinopathy.

Packet-supported premises follow. Insoluble TDP-43 aggregates associate with nuclear-pore and transport components, and disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental systems, with related pore pathology in ALS tissue [S1]. Nucleoporin phosphorylation stays unidentified and unordered [S1]. Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA alters RanGAP localization and impairs nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons; transport or repeat-RNA manipulations can modify model phenotypes [S2]. That route is genetic-context-specific and leaves nucleoporin phosphorylation unestablished [S2]. Cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form without conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport proteins, and accompany import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and cell death; de-mixing drives that import inhibition and nuclear loss [S3]. Phosphorylated TDP-43 in those assemblies is a modification of TDP-43 [S3]. Cellular stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs transport, and altering stress-granule assembly can modify transport defects and disease-model phenotypes [S4].

Speculative bridges. No supplied source names NUP98, CDK1, a residue list, or TDP-43 M337V. Unverified prior knowledge: NUP98 forms part of the FG barrier; CDK1 phosphorylates NUP98 during mitotic pore remodeling; M337V is a disease-linked TDP-43 mutation; G3BP1/2 scaffold stress granules; FG phosphorylation is typically multi-site. Assumption: after mitosis, M337V-linked stress reactivates a residual CDK1 pool that binds pore-resident NUP98; locked-cluster occupancy then slows karyopherin import while phospho-NUP98 remains in the pore. A kinase other than CDK1 recovered on NUP98 revises the initiating mechanism.

Causal order. TDP-43 pathology is the upstream context [S1]. Before the mark, the assay must show post-mitotic CDK1 activity and CDK1 bound to NUP98. Cluster phosphorylation on pore-localized NUP98 is the initiating pore event and precedes nuclear TDP-43 loss. Selective import failure, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and neuronal death follow. The mark-before-assemblies order is an assumption in tension with [S3], where assembly-associated TDP-43 phosphorylation is a timed marker. Alternatives are stress-granule sequestration [S4], C9orf72-linked RanGAP mislocalization [S2], nucleoporin departure from pores [S1], and parallel stress in which the phosphate and import failure co-occur while the phosphate is dispensable.

Discriminating test. Phase one compares post-mitotic TDP-43 M337V iPSC-derived neurons and an inducible cytoplasmic TDP-43 system aligned with [S3] to isogenic controls, starting before nuclear TDP-43 loss. Each interval measures CDK1 activity and CDK1 recruitment to NUP98, then nuclear-envelope mass spectrometry locks the earliest occupied FG-repeat residues and a pre-declared minimum site-occupancy rule. Design readouts, outside the packet: facilitated import is the nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio of an SV40 large-T NLS fluorescent cargo, and passive permeability is nuclear entry of a size-excluded inert dextran. The pre-declared lead, fixed before unblinding, is one sampling interval of import failure before nuclear TDP-43 loss. Those samples score phospho-NUP98 pore localization, TDP-43 assembly and nuclear-cytoplasmic distribution, nucleoporin localization [S1], stress-granule transport factors, and a pre-declared death count as neuronal dysfunction.

Phase two starts only after the residue list and occupancy rule are locked. Inducible replacement is restricted to post-mitotic neurons, with mitosis already finished, using non-phosphorylatable or phosphomimetic alleles at the locked sites. Allele results count only after edited NUP98 replaces endogenous protein in assembled pores at matched dosage, incorporation, and pore density, with facilitated import scored separately from passive leak. A post-mitotic CDK1 degradation or inhibition arm leaves the NUP98 sequence unchanged. A crossed arm co-depletes G3BP1 and G3BP2. A C9orf72-repeat arm [S2] asks whether the locked cluster is required outside M337V.

Pore initiation predicts a CDK1 signal before pore-localized cluster occupancy, NLS-import failure with phospho-NUP98 still in the pore, rescue of NLS import by the non-phosphorylatable allele, and NLS-import failure from the phosphomimetic allele without passive leak. G3BP1/2 co-depletion tests sequestration [S4]: restored import with the cluster still occupied favors sequestration. Assembly counts place [S3] assemblies before, after, or beside the mark.

Separate falsifiers follow. Timing: facilitated import fails at the pre-declared lead while assembled-pore cluster occupancy is still absent. Necessity: an unoccupied cluster, at matched incorporation, dosage, and pore density, leaves facilitated-import failure and neuronal death intact on every stress-granule background, with granules present and after G3BP1/2 co-depletion. Phosphomimetic: matched post-mitotic phosphomimetic NUP98 leaves NLS import intact and passive leak unchanged. Localization: phospho-NUP98 has left the pore when import fails. CDK1: recruitment of a different NUP98-bound writer revises the initiating mechanism; CDK1 loss that leaves cluster occupancy and import failure intact, or that clears the cluster while import failure remains.

Limitations. iPSC-neuron timing leaves the ALS-tissue and sporadic sequence unresolved [S1]. CDK1, M337V, G3BP1/2, and the cluster remain assumptions until mapping and the recruitment assay lock them. Phosphomimetics approximate regulated phosphates roughly. Intact-animal studies and treatment tests lie outside this design.

author: grok
critique: The initiating event is not a concrete target: CDK5 and an unnamed set of at most four NUP98 FG SP/TP motifs are assumptions with no residue list, occupancy assay, or packet anchor, and a future passive-probe result is treated as what would make that bridge supported. Lock exact residues or a pre-specified mapping rule and assay before the timing study, and keep CDK5 as one kinase arm rather than the pre-committed cause.

The in-place selectivity mechanism is not isolated from NUP98 leaving the pore. Envelope retention is scored only for NUP107 and NUP133, so a phosphomimetic leak is still compatible with mitotic-style NUP98 release, which the writeup sets aside. Measure NUP98 and phospho-NUP98 at the envelope in the same bins, and falsify the assembled-pore claim if import failure occurs only when pore-localized NUP98 falls.

The discriminating test is not executable as written and one arm is confounded. Induction is only arsenite-free, stress-kinase and death gates and the passive-probe size cutoff are unnamed, the one-bin lead is not a constant interval on the 0/2/6/12/24 h grid, and phosphomimetics are read in G3BP1/2-disrupted cells even though S4 shows that altering stress-granule assembly itself changes transport. Name the assembly induction, occupancy method, probe size, and numeric gates, and add a G3BP-intact granule-negative mimetic arm plus a disruption-only control.

author: grok
critique: CDK5 and “at most four” NUP98 FG-region SP/TP motifs are pre-committed without residue numbers, an occupancy assay, or a CDK5 necessity arm, so another proline-directed kinase could produce the same occupancy pattern and still count as support. Name the pre-registered residues, define the occupancy measurement, and either drop CDK5 from the causal claim or require CDK5 loss-of-function in the same bins before that kinase bridge is treated as tested.

The clock starts from arsenite-free cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies, but the induction method, assembly criterion, and numeric G3BP1 and stress-kinase cutoffs are unspecified, while the write-up still calls NUP98 phosphorylation an early initiator of the cascade that the protocol places downstream of those assemblies. Specify an S3-matched induction and those exclusion thresholds, and state the chain as assembly formation, then NUP98 phosphorylation, then barrier failure and nuclear TDP-43 loss, with scaffold exit and transport-factor sequestration as later amplifiers.

The passive-permeability rise is the result that would link FG-repeat charge to selectivity loss, yet probe size and chemistry are undefined, and phosphomimetic import failure that coincides with TNPO1 or RanGAP sequestration has no assigned call. Define the inert probe and its exclusion cutoff, and pre-assign that mixed outcome to the sequestration alternative so it cannot be scored as support for a pore-intrinsic mechanism.

critique: The ranked item reports PMIDs as none, so the final claim is detached from the four records the argument uses. Attach PMIDs 29311743, 26308891, 30853299, and 29628143 as boundary evidence and mark the NUP98–CDK1–FG-cluster step as unsupported by those records.

The initiating event is an unnamed FG-repeat cluster whose occupancy rule is deferred, and recovery of another NUP98-bound writer is defined as a revision of the same hypothesis. Pre-state a numeric minimum occupancy and a sampling interval, and treat a non-CDK1 writer as falsifying the CDK1-initiation clause.

Phase one runs M337V iPSC neurons and an inducible cytoplasmic TDP-43 system with no decision rule for discordant timelines, and assembly-before-phosphorylation stays only a noted tension with S3. Declare the post-mitotic M337V series decisive, and count facilitated-import failure already present while assembled-pore cluster occupancy is absent, including when S3-like assemblies are already scored, as falsifying initiation.

Phase-two allele replacement requires mutant NUP98 to occupy already assembled pores after mitosis has ended, with no exchange method and no numeric bounds. S3 is rendered as de-mixing driving import failure, which is stronger than the packet's association wording, and the lead interval plus death endpoint stay undefined. Attribute the stronger causal verb to the paper title as a claim under test, and pre-declare clock times and the death assay so order and dysfunction can be falsified.
